projects.summary: 中文说明： AI 编程助手（Claude Code / Codex）最大的问题往往不是能力，而是纪律：不问清需求直接开写、修 bug 靠瞎试、嘴上说"测试通过了"其实没跑过、上个会话拍板的目标下个会话就忘。 coding-discipline 是一个「护栏」插件——不接管工作流，平时安静，具名失败模式临近才介入： 按需触发的 8 条纪律 skill：设计先行（brainstorming）、红绿重构（tdd）、先根因再修（systematic-debugging）、优先级评审（code-review）、拿证据再说"做完了"（verify-before-done）、git 流程（git-flow）、上下文卫生（context-hygiene）、spec 同步（spec-sync）。日常小改动零打扰。 spec-sync（这个项目自有的一层）：把对话里已确认的目标 / 非目标 / 硬约束 / 验收标准写回项目已有文档，不新增任何制品，下个会话不再把否掉的方案重做一遍。 固定注入被 CI 冻结：每会话固定上下文约 1.2k tokens，文案变大直接挂 CI——「轻」是一条会失败的测试，不是口号。 跨平台：同一份 SKILL.md 同时服务 Claude Code 和 Codex；hook 纯 bash 无 jq 依赖，Windows / Git Bash 有独立测试。 英文为主 + 完整中文 README：v0.8.1 起产品面英文优先（便于全球分发），README.zh-CN.md 全文维护。理念致谢英文的 superpowers（MIT）。 MIT 协议。欢迎试用和提 issue——尤其欢迎「该触发没触发 / 不该触发触发了」的反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: Docs.dev – A docs site you own, where AI drafts and you edit in place
projects.author: linktothenew
projects.summary:
Hi HN. Some backstory, because it explains why this exists. Our startup originally worked on AI-assisted documentation generation. When Claude Code and Cursor's agents matured, we asked ourselves the uncomfortable question: does a standalone "AI writes your docs" product still need to exist? We concluded no, and pivoted to what's now keyboard.dev. That left us with the docs.dev domain. We had a buyer in the docs space lined up and were genuinely excited for it to have a proper home. A month later, they changed their mind. So instead of letting a domain we loved sit parked, we built the docs platform we'd always wanted as a side project. The workflow it's built around: coding agents already write documentation well, but reviewing agent-written docs in raw MDX is miserable. So with docs.dev, Claude Code updates your docs template in the same session where it ships your code (the template carries a CLAUDE.md and skills, so it knows the conventions). Then you go to your actual docs site, on your domain, log in as an admin, and review the page exactly as readers will see it. Anything the AI got wrong, you edit or delete in place, directly on the live site. Publishing is a git commit to your repo, and CI redeploys. The same URL serves readers and, for admins, becomes the editor. The economics are the other half of the pitch. There's no hosting on our side and no content database: one click clones the template into your GitHub account and deploys it to your Cloudflare account with push-to-deploy CI. AI writing, image generation, and chat run on Cloudflare's own primitives (Workers AI and friends), billed at Cloudflare's rates on your account. You're not paying a docs vendor to host your own documentation, and you're not paying their markup on AI calls. The optional docs.dev service adds exactly one thing, team sign-in, and it's a sign-in check, not a dependency: if we disappear tomorrow, your site keeps serving. We deliberately built on existing technology rather than reinventing it: Fumadocs (Next.js + MDX) for the docs framework, chenglou's pretext layout engine for the reading experience (prose flows around figures like a magazine spread, while the server still renders plain indexable

text for crawlers and no-JS readers), and Cloudflare's out-of-the-box platform pieces for deploys, CI, and AI. Honest caveats: it requires the Cloudflare Workers Paid plan ($5/mo) because the server Worker is ~5.3 MiB gzipped, over the free plan's 1 MiB limit. It's a side project, not our main company. And the magazine-style layout is the kind of thing you either love or find gratuitous. We'd genuinely like to hear which. There's a walkthrough video on the homepage if you'd rather watch the workflow than read it. Happy to answer questions about the agent workflow, the in-place editing, the ownership model, or the pivot. Note it is an early but hope this helps people that wants easy, cheap, and effective documentation on their terms

projects.title: [开源推荐] NeuroBook：面向长篇小说创作的多 Agent 写作 IDE。
projects.author: notnotype
projects.summary: AI 能写好一段文字，但写不好一部长篇： 写长了就吃书：设定靠模型的对话记忆，越写越漂移——上一卷断掉的手臂，这一卷自己长回来了。 挖的坑忘了填：第 3 章埋的伏笔第 200 章还没收；AI 的思路一关对话就蒸发，作者的便签三个月就找不到。 一股 AI 味：填充词、机械过渡、公式化排比，读者一眼识破。 工具是散的：Word 写正文、Obsidian 管设定、网页聊天框讨论剧情——三个工具，三份数据，互相不认识；AI 的思路一关对话就蒸发。 NeuroBook 把这些当作工程问题来解决——设定、剧情、正文、世界状态都是 workspace 里可见的文件，作者和 Agent 在明确权限内共同维护。 亮点 四大核心能力 🌍 World Engine：不吃书的世界状态引擎 长篇最大的敌人是设定漂移。World Engine 用「时间线 + 切面」做事件溯源：每个重要时间点记录一次状态变更，任意时刻的世界状态都由之前的切面推算得出——角色三个月前受的伤、王国十年前的国库存量，随时可查、不会漂移。补设定就是在合适的时间点插入一个切面，倒叙和回忆天然支持。 世界结构自己定义（Zod schema）：人物、门派、王国、大陆都可以是有状态的 subject（主体）。 可以获取任何时间的 subject 状态 历法自定义：现实公历、简化纪年或完全架空的历法都支持，公元前也能算。 每次变更都是带时间戳的可审计记录；他什么时候获得了这把剑完全可以审计出来 Agent 沙箱读写分权：leader 可写、writer 只读，写作时不会误改世界。 🧵 Plot Workbench：剧情工坊——伏笔有账本，决策有存档 结构归结构，因果归因果：承载树管故事在哪讲（卷 → 章），因果树管故事为什么发生（剧情线 → 场景）。倒叙、插叙、多线随便排，因果链永远清晰。 承诺系统：每个伏笔都是对读者的承诺——埋下、推进、兑现全程记账，节拍挂在场景上随剧情自动更新，写到目标章自动进入写作指令。契诃夫说挂在墙上的枪必须响，NeuroBook 负责提醒你它还没响。不止伏笔——感情线想每隔几章发一次糖？也记上，它会提醒你已经三十章没发糖了。 创作决策记录：三个月前为什么让主角黑化？翻回去只有结果、没有理由，想改又不敢改——Decision 记得：决策当场记档，风险必填，推翻也留痕。 章节信息控制：读者知道什么、主角知道什么、必须隐瞒什么、只能暗示什么——希区柯克的悬念理论，做成了字段。 场景直接锚定世界时间轴、地点和出场角色，剧情规划与世界状态互相咬合。 ✍️ 多 Agent 写作工作室：好马配好鞍 AI 已经是一匹好马，NeuroBook 是那副鞍（NeuroAgentHarness——Harness 本义就是马具），缰绳在你手里。目前的 AI 没有独立写完一本优质小说的能力，但它最擅长的恰恰是：整理资料、查证细节、陪你头脑风暴、给你泼冷水——一个人写作最难熬的不是难，是孤独，现在有搭子了。 各司其职：leader 规划剧情与调度，writer 专职正文，retrieval / researcher 查设定查资料——数值不乱编（引擎账上有），资料不瞎猜（researcher 去查）。 默认写作主链：灵感探索 → 项目与世界书初始化 → World Engine 建档 → 剧情规划与状态推进 → 章节写作 → 写后回补。 三模式：讨论模式只出主意不动稿，计划模式先给完整方案、批准才执行；每次模式切换都要你点头。 编辑器内 Inline AI：选中即改、流式预览、不打断主编辑流、不占用主会话。 🧹 llmlint：给文字做 lint，去掉 AI 味 像 eslint 检查代码一样检查稿件。340 条规则覆盖填充词、机械过渡、公式化设问、二元对比、空泛总结、节奏单调等典型 AI 写作痕迹；静态规则秒级扫全稿，LLM 规则做语境判断，机械问题支持自动修复。既是编辑器里的润色 Skill，也是独立 projects.title: Show HN: Nully – FOSS AI chat without the bloat
projects.author: johnfahey
projects.summary: As someone who doesn't use any of the more "advanced" features on sites like ChatGPT or Claude (agentic mode, memory, image generation, deep research, etc), I found the bloat of these services, both in UX and in performance, to be pretty tedious. There are a million AI chat interfaces out there, but I could never find one that just did simple messaging and history in the most minimal and lightweight way possible. So I made my own. Nully is written in Go and Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. It literally just sends messages to OpenRouter, receives the result, and stores your messages locally. It's very simple, very clean, and very lightweight (see performance graphs on the site). It has basic chat features, basic model settings, and works with just about any OpenRouter text model. It supports attachments and basic web search via the OpenRouter API. I made Nully mostly for myself, but the cost to open-source it and host it on a cheap VPS is practically nothing, so I figured I'd release it if it can help anyone else. I don't make any revenue off of it, and have no desire to. There's no accounts, no subscriptions, and no proxies or middlemen (other than OpenRouter of course). You can export all of your chats to JSON, and everything stays on your local machine. It's 100% open source and self-hostable if you want that too. Let me know what you think!

projects.title: Show HN: Bike4Mind – open-core AI workbench; any model, agents, RAG, self-host
projects.author: erikbethke
projects.summary: Hi HN, I am Erik Bethke, game dev that has been making online games for 30+ years (Starfleet Command, GoPets, FarmVille, Mafia Wars). For the last 3 years I have been building Bike4Mind and now I have to put my big boy pants on and 'go to market'. Ugh, it would be so much more cozy to fire up a few more agents and fix a few more bugs, polish some more UX - or hey how about a new feature that does Q, R or S? What is Bike4Mind? I started Bike4Mind to be the home of a bunch of AI augmented game development tools, and over time have just kept adding features. It is a full cognitive workbench we have all of the features - notebooks, files, data lakes & RAG, agents (different forms), generate share-able artifacts in react or python. We have secure websockets to connect to our CLI - B4M CLI, so it is truly batteries included - and runs any model - OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Bedrock. Switch models during a conversation, fork a notebook, run 4 different models on the same prompt, loads of image generation support, and import OpenAI and Anthropic history and of course egress with your own at any time. So, all of the models and all the features. Sure, but so what? We are huge believers in infrastructure as code and leveraged SSTv4, and Bike4Mind is able to 100% self-host on your own hardware. You can run Qwen locally and have all of the GUI and CLI and be totally offline from the internet. The most complete fully-sovereign workbench I've found - and if you know a more complete one I'd genuinely like to see it. Okay, so all of the models, features and I can self host - sounds cool, but why don't I vibe that up myself in Fable or such right? We have used this with our enterprise clients over the last 3 years and so you also get all of the Enterprise SaaS stuff - batteries included - multi-tenant, RBAC, MFA, throttling, moderation, analytics, premium subscriptions, credits, heck even a slim CRM is built in! OAuth, github, google docs, notion, etc etc… it is one thing to lick the cupcake and get that MVP up and running and working for you - it is a totally different beast putting something that you can deploy for an enterprise. What? What are you doing exactly? 48 hours ago (July 5th noon Austin) we took everything we built and we made it open with the most progressive license I could lay out: Source immediately under a BSL 1.1 license with a one-way ratchet where after 24 months each release converts to full Apache-2.0. Please appreciate that this is an irrevocable, one-way ratchet where Bike4Mind just gets more open with each release and each month. This is not a "Hey we are open source until well cough reasons - jazz hands we are closed - thanks for all of the PRs!" To be clear, I know that source-available is not the same as open-source. But check out our actual license and the marketing site - we encourage and permit anyone to fork and create new products and sell them, or take the whole thing and self-host on their own AWS account or their own hardware. You can also fork it and customize a full stack AI solution for your own clients. Really the only thing we are holding back - and just over 24 months - is not allowing people to stand up a vanilla copy of Bike4Mind and compete with B4M-as-a-service or change the name and do the same.

projects.summary: Lenormand.live是一个专为神秘学与雷诺曼（Lenormand）爱好者打造的在线占卜、自学与能量梳解平台。区别于市面上大多架构陈旧、交互生硬的同类工具，本项目采用极简的 纯前端处理 + WebAssembly (Wasm) + AI 动态解牌的硬核现代技术栈，在彻底免除后端服务器负担的同时，为用户提供极其丰富、丝滑且深度定制的交互体验。 🌐 🛠️ 网站技术特点 作为一个纯技术驱动的独立开发项目，我们在工程实现和用户体验上做到了以下极致： 极致性能与零开销：核心业务逻辑和算法全部引入 WebAssembly (Wasm) 跑在纯前端，不仅降低了服务端的计算开销，更让高并发下的响应速度达到毫秒级，实现真正的单页无缝切换。 极其丝滑的现代动效：基于 Next.js、Tailwind CSS 与 Framer Motion，我们为传统的洗牌、抽牌、展牌和侧边交互面板定制了流畅的物理动画效果，体验完全不输原生 App。 智能上下文解牌（AI-Powered）：结合大语言模型 API，针对用户输入的具体困惑和问题上下文进行动态、结构化的牌阵解读，告别市面上死板、千篇一律的固定文本拼接。 🔮 核心功能与对比优势 对比目前网络上现有的基础同类占卜站点（如 lenormand.life 等），Lenormand.live 在功能丰富度上进行了全方位的深度优化，不仅支持全语种无缝切换，更一次性集成了 10 大核心牌阵与高频交互组件，全方位满足从“小白浅尝”到“核心极客”的各种测算需求： 1. 高频互动与轻量决策（泛流量捕获利器）： 每日运势（Daily Guidance）：单牌流直观交互，提供每日能量指引。 是/否占卜（Yes/No Reading）：针对非黑即白的纠结问题，提供即时明晰的判定逻辑。 决策指引（Decision Making）：多路径对比交互，为用户的现实选择提供结构化参考。 2. 多维深度经典牌阵（硬核占卜实力）： 线性牌阵（Linear Spread）：经典 3 牌/5 牌流，精准梳理事件的因果脉络。 十字牌阵（Cross Spread）：多轴向交织，深入解构现状核心、潜意识与外部阻碍。 九宫格牌阵（3x3 Block Spread）：提供九位一体的立体视角，全方位捕捉时间与空间交错的丰富信息。 大蓝图牌阵（Grand Tableau）：雷诺曼神秘学的“终极试金石”，全量卡牌悉数登场，考验纯前端在大数据图谱下的丝滑渲染与联动交互。 黄道十二宫牌阵（Astrological Houses Spread）：无缝融合古典占星体系，划分十二生活领域，提供跨度更长、宏观深度的年运/半年运势总览。 3. 定制化场景与组合技术（AI 动态深度解牌）： 爱情占卜（Love & Relationships）：针对当代年轻群体的头号精神内耗场景（如断联、复联、复合、暧昧）进行专项文案和交互优化。 牌组合解读（Card Combinations）：雷诺曼的核心灵魂在于“两两成词”。我们基于 AI 建立了强大的多牌复合动态解牌引擎，彻底告别死板、千篇一律的固定文本拼接。 ⚙️ 后续矩阵规划 目前我们已经打通了这套高效率、低成本的纯前端神秘学交互模版，后续会将该硬核架构克隆至更多垂直类神秘学项目中，构建完整的全量矩阵： lenormand.live（雷诺曼） geomancy.live（极客地占术） mayakin.live（玛雅十三月亮历） itarot.live（AI 塔罗） tradastro.com（古典占星） 💬 一句话推荐 "Lenormand.live 用最现代的前端技术和丝滑交互，为传统神秘学工具换上‘极客内核’。不仅牌阵更全、体验更佳，更是一次纯前端 Wasm 降本增效的极佳实战尝试，欢迎大家体验和交流探讨！"

projects.title: Show HN: Wayflow – an embeddable AI workflow builder (open source)
projects.author: tahazsh
projects.summary: Hi! I’m Taha. In many agentic products that support workflows (including one I worked on), I noticed they either don’t support node-based editors, or use React Flow and go through the difficult work of integrating it into their product to run it and work with their existing logic. So I thought about creating a tool that could help with this by closing the gap between the editor and the runtime. That’s why I created Wayflow. The basic architecture is simple: you just need to create a graph (which is a JSON object) that the runtime knows how to run. The runtime doesn’t care where that graph is coming from, it just needs the right schema. And with the help of the editor, you can create the graph, and then export it or directly save it on your backend in your database. And then when you want to execute it, you just hand it to the runtime. The runtime can either stream the execution (which is useful for the editor), or give you the final result. How you execute the graph is up to you: through an API endpoint, a cron job, or any other way you want. Wayflow comes with a number of built-in nodes like Input, Output, LLM, Image Generation, Array Operations, Conditional, ... and I spent a lot of time making sure they cover most of the common cases your app needs. But you can easily add your custom nodes that work for your specific app. One of the main challenges (and one of the fun parts) was making it provider-neutral. So it’s not locked to a specific LLM provider. I did this by targeting the OpenAI-compatible API, which almost all frontier models support. The same thing for frameworks and libraries. It has zero dependencies and it’s framework-agnostic. There are many things I didn’t cover here, like tool calling, converting full workflows into tools, human-in-the-loop, etc. You can read all about this in the docs. One important thing I’d like to mention is that even though LLMs are a huge part of the workflows you create, they are completely optional. You can literally build any workflow (with the help of more custom nodes) with zero AI, for full deterministic execution. You can try it in your browser (no signup, bring your own key) at https://wayflow.build . It’s also on npm (`npm install wayflow`), and the code is on GitHub ( https://github.com/TahaSh/wayflow ). I hope this is something you’ll find helpful to use in your projects. Happy coding!

projects.title: 【工具自荐】LinkExtractor：隐私优先的文件批量链接提取/验证/导出工具
projects.author: isixe
projects.summary: 工具介绍 LinkExtractor 是一个用于批量提取、验证和导出链接。所有处理均在浏览器本地完成，不上传任何数据到服务器。 在日常开发和内容整理中，经常需要从各种文件（如 HTML、Markdown、JSON、CSV、代码文件等）中批量提取 URL，然后逐条验证其可用性。LinkExtractor 将这一流程整合为一步到位的高效体验。 核心功能 批量链接提取 — 支持从纯文本及多种文件格式（TXT、JSON、MD、HTML、XML、CSV、JS、TS、JSX、TSX）中自动提取所有链接 链接验证 — 5 线程并发检查每个链接的可用性，检测成功、失败和超时，附带 HTTP 状态码 多格式导出 — 结果可导出为 TXT、JSON 或 CSV，适用于数据分析、文档和报告 智能筛选 — 按状态（全部、有效、无效、等待中）筛选链接 重新验证 — 无需重新提取，即可单独重试失败的链接 域名分组 — 按域名对链接分组，便于浏览和分类 搜索 — 在已提取的链接中搜索指定 URL 黑名单链接 - 通配符形式忽略提取的链接 适用场景 网站迁移/改版后批量检测死链 从书签或收藏文件中整理可用的链接资源 从代码仓库中提取所有外部引用链接进行审计 内容创作者整理引用的参考来源并验证有效性 SEO 分析和外链管理

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Continuum：一句话生成同一主角出演的连续 AI 短剧，跨集人物不漂移
projects.author: calderbuild
projects.summary: 给一个剧情设定和一个主角，它自动写剧本、拆分镜、用 AI 生成竖屏短剧，并且同一个主角在多集之间形象保持一致。 做 AI 短剧最难的不是生成单个镜头，而是连续性——换一集、换一个镜头，主角的脸、发型、穿着就漂了。Continuum 的做法是让一个 agent 维护一份「剧集圣经」(Series Bible)，把主角的标准形象锁死，再注入到每一集、每一个镜头的生成里，所以跨集身份能对得上。 上图是同一个主角在两集、四个差异很大的镜头里的样子。用 Qwen-VL 当评委给一致性打分，在这条演示剧集上跨集身份一致性 0.98。 一组 agent 沿流水线协作：编剧写本 → 拆分镜 → 摄影生成每个镜头 → 评委打分、不合格就进优化循环重渲染 → 剪辑拼接并烧录字幕。前端有一个实时「控制室」，把每个 agent 正在做的事流式展示出来。这些 agent 同时也暴露成了 MCP 工具，可以让别的 Agent 直接调用这套流水线。 技术栈：Qwen3 写剧本与优化提示词，Wan 生成 9:16 竖屏视频，Qwen-VL 做一致性评委；后端 Python + FastAPI（SSE 流式），剪辑用 ffmpeg。 自部署，自带 DashScope API Key 即可运行，MIT 开源。

projects.title: Show HN: Emra – A workspace where every app you build shares one db
projects.author: thejarren
projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm really excited to share Emra with you. The yc description would be: It's like "Notion meets Lovable". It's a workspace where you build full apps using AI and every app sits on one shared database and service layer. Generated apps are always editable, and (coming soon:) can interact with each other in the workspace. I'm of the opinion that the cost of software will go rapidly to zero (I don't think that's too surprising to any of you), but there will always be room for effort and creativity. Emra is essentially built for the future where every person is a developer. Essentially personal software for everyone. So far I've built notes apps with a 3d graph view to see connections, a video editing app and a canvas design tool (figma clone) with export capabilities, as well as a collection of project management tools and games. Right now the most satisfying thing is being able to fix a bug I run into in around the same amount of time that it takes to send a bug report in any traditional app. We're using the best models to make this work at the moment. Basically anything Opus 4.6 or later, as far as I'm concerned is the baseline of what we can use to make this happen. Our agent is currently only capable of building, though that will change rapidly, and we are pretty proud that our build loop is more token efficient than using Claude Code or other harnesses. Arguably we are in the same category as Dreamer (Meta acquired) or Wabi (raised $20m), but at the moment we're bootstrapped and working to deliver as much value to users as possible. Users will be soon be able to download their data and apps at any time (I like to think of it as extending obsidians "file over app" philosophy to file+app). In general, I think for a platform like this to exist, we want to be as value aligned with users as possible. So our focus is on providing a solid service layer that abstracts away the complexity of most modern full stack applications. Ideally, people using Emra pay for hosting or usage and we earn our spot rather than locking you in. On the technical side, we feel good right now. We know there will be some scaling + security challenges, but honestly, our biggest hurdle at the moment is rebuilding existing applications in a way that makes them actually worth using inside of Emra, basically solving that blank page problem. We are building apps on an SDK that we plan on open sourcing over the next month or so, and will also provide a CLI tool so people can build Emra apps inside of Claude Code or other agents (this is how we are actually building many of our app store apps). I'm also still trying to nail down the messaging. Initially I had planned on aggressively focusing on consumer, but the cost to build an app is still prohibitive, so we're going to keep testing different approaches. We're still very early, so I'd really appreciate any honest feedback. And I'm happy to answer any questions you might have.

projects.title: Show HN: Gist Discover – TikTok for ArXiv Summaries
projects.author: MediaSquirrel
projects.summary: Dunno about you, but I cannot keep up with the volume of AI research. Reading one paper properly takes 30–60 minutes, and it's hard to know which are even worth it. I built Gist, an AI summarizer for ADHD brains. Each paper is a clean slide deck with four layers you move through: 1. the Gist – the whole idea 1-2 sentences 2. Logic – breakdown of the argument + evidence in discrete ideas 3. Counter-Argument – strongest argument against the author (AI generated) 4. Steelman – transcendent rebuttal to the counter-argument (AI generated) There's integrated TTS audio too — hit play to listen. I went overboard and post-trained a model specifically for this. When I say I went overboard, I really did! I burned $130k of AWS Claude credits on the dataset, 1/3rd of which is Arxiv papers. My goal was to absolutely max out on data quality over quantity. And it worked! I started with a looping 5-step multi-teacher editorial pipeline using Claude Opus 4.6 & Gemini 3.1 Pro, then distilled it into Gemini 2.5 Flash single shot model that (according to my evals) beats all the best single-shot frontier model for this task on quality (while being 20x faster and 10x cheaper). Here's a random one from the feed right now: Qwen-Image-Agent: Bridging the Context Gap in Real-World Image Generation Qwen-Image-Agent scores 45.4 on a benchmark where the direct image generator it's built on scores 17.4 — a 161% improvement from the same model, same weights, same prompt. The difference isn't better pixels. It's a system that asks "What else do you need?" before it ever draws a single one. gist.is/discover is a free feed of all the arXiv papers I've run through it. No signup. Right now, the feed is totally random, but if this gets traction I'll build a proper recommendation system. Read the gist in ~10 seconds and go deeper if you want (inc going straight to the source), or tap Next→ and try again. I also created Gist Discover extensions for your IDE so you can read / listen / learn while your AI agents work. Cursor/Windsurf: https://open-vsx.org/extension/Transcendence/gist-discover VS Code: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Transcen... Feedback welcome! Enjoy! -Matt

projects.title: 【开源自荐】一款完全开源的无限画布Open Canvas，支持用自己的API key生图生视频
projects.author: ZeroLu
projects.summary: 经常折腾 AI 的老玩家们可能还记得，前段时间社区里非常火的 libtv（或者 tapnow）这类工作流画布工具。它们用直观的连线、节点化操作，把“文本生成-图片生成-视频动画”串联在一起，体验确实非常惊艳： 不过，惊艳归惊艳，每次玩这类工具时，我的钱包都在隐隐作痛。 例如LibTV，以充一个高级会员699一万一积分算的话，你生成一个image2模型的2k图是60积分一张图，换成人民币大概3.5元一张图。 这个定价真是图片刺客！因为生成GPT Image 2的图片在Cyberbara只需要几毛钱。对于我们这种喜欢搞实验、天天高频测试的 AI 创作者和开发者来说，这种“高昂的过路费”实在是让人束手束脚，根本没办法放开手脚去创作。 既然如此，为什么不自己做一个？ 于是，我花了两个礼拜，做了一个 完全开源、本地优先（Local-first）、支持自带 Key（BYOK） 的工作流画布项目——Open Canvas。 今天，我把它分享出来，希望能给同样喜欢折腾的大家提供一个更自由、成本更低的创作解法。 GitHub 开源项目官网： 为什么要做 Open Canvas？它有什么不一样？ 简单来说，Open Canvas 的目标很纯粹：把主动权还给用户。 1. 本地优先，数据全在自己手里 它不需要你绑定任何云端大厂的账号，也不依赖复杂的数据库。你的所有画布、连线数据和运行记录，都会以 JSON 格式保存在本地（open-canvas-db.json），支持一键导入和导出。如果你有便宜的API，直接用就可以。 2. 功能完善，模型齐全 目前支持 Note（便签）、Text（文本）、Image（图片）、Video（视频）和 Audio（音频）节点。支持市面上主流provider的各类模型的输入输出。 3. 上游输出，下游自动注入 这是最爽的一点。你不需要手动复制上一节点的图片链接去喂给下一个视频节点。Open Canvas 会自动解析连线，把上游的图片或文本自动注入到下游的视频/图像生成模型中，实现无缝的工作流自动化。 核心亮点：把创作成本打到“几分钱”的 Cyberbara API 既然是“自带 Key（BYOK）”，那么接入什么 API 决定了你的钱包厚度。 我特别推荐大家配置 Cyberbara API（ GPT Image 2：生图效果极其惊艳，但价格只要几毛钱一张！相比 libtv 动辄几块钱的单张生图成本，在这里你可以毫无压力地批量生图。 Gemini Omni Video：来自谷歌的高质量模型，同样只要几毛钱一条，生成流畅度和细节保留都处于第一梯队。 Grok Imagine Video：马斯克的“无限制”模型，不仅动力澎湃，更重要的是支持 NSFW，给前沿创作者提供了难得的无限制创作空间。 最方便的是，只需要一把 Cyberbara API Key，就能同时覆盖“生图 + 生视频 + 资源上传/对象存储”的全套流程，免去了满世界找各种第三方 S3 存储和申请不同平台的痛苦。 跑个案例：如何用它串起一套完整工作流？ 为了让大家更直观地感受这套工作流的爽快感，我们用一个之前在X上爆火的手绘红线生成FPV穿越机运镜视频的案例来串一下。 1️⃣ 第一步：生成或准备一张高清底图 你可以直接上传一张自己的合照，或者在 Image 节点中输入以下这串Prompt 来生成底图： Prompt： Photorealistic fashion shot of five diverse women in a luxury modern penthouse. Bright natural light from large windows, city view, dark wood floors, beige sofa, marble wall. Front left: redhead lying down in black top, plaid skirt, heels. Back left: black-haired woman on sofa arm in black top and shorts. Center: blonde on sofa in white shirt, beige shorts. Front right: Black woman sitting on rug in beige vest and shorts. Back right: Black woman in black top and long beige skirt. Cinematic, 8k, highly detailed. 点击运行，稍等片刻，一张超高画质、极具电影感的五人闺蜜合照就生成好了。 2️⃣ 第二步：在画布上“手绘运镜轨迹” 这步是灵魂！普通的图生视频工具，镜头往哪移全凭 AI 抽卡。而在 Open Canvas 里，你可以“画”出运镜轨迹。 1. 点击图片下方的内置编辑工具（Edit Tool）。 2. 直接在图片上用红色的导向线画一条你想要的运镜轨迹。比如从左到右划过，或者从背景推向前景。 3. 这条红线，就是等会儿摄像机的运动轨迹。 3️⃣ 第三步：连线 Video 节点并完成生成 现在，拉出一条连线，将你的 Image 节点连到 Video 节点。 为了达到完美的运镜效果，请进行以下关键设置： 比例：16:9 分辨率：720P 时长：15秒 注意：由于图片中包含大量写实的人脸，为了防止转视频时脸部崩坏，请在模型选项中务必选择 “Seedance 2.0 Stable” 模型。 在 Video 节点的 Prompt 框中，输入这行镜头控制指令： Video Prompt： FPV shot. The camera follows the motion path of the red guide line, the red line must not be visible in the final footage. 运行！Open Canvas 会自动解析你的图片以及你在上面画的那条红线，并自动抹除画面中的红色参考线。 出来的视频效果会让你惊掉下巴：镜头顺着你手画的红色轨迹，极其丝滑、自然地游走在房间里，每个人物的面部和身体动态自然无崩坏，简直就像是一部精心调色后的电影预告片！ 。 如何开始使用？（提供 3 种姿势） 为了照顾不同折腾程度的玩家，我准备了三种体验方式： 姿势一：直接访问已部署的在线 BYOK 版（最推荐 ⚡️） 如果你不想折腾本地环境，但想用自己的 API Key 体验低成本生成的快感： 1. 电脑浏览器直接打开： 2. 点击右上角的 Providers 按钮。 3. 填入你的 Cyberbara API Key（可在 注册后直接免费获取）。 4. 新建画布，直接开玩！ 姿势二：小白极简无脑版（免 Key、免配置 ☁️） 如果你觉得配置 API Key 还是太麻烦，只想直接上手玩画布： 直接访问： 这是 Cyberbara 官方托管的 Canvas 产品，不需要生成和配置 API Key，开箱即用，最适合不想折腾的小白用户。 姿势三：本地部署、完全自托管（开发者专属 🛠️） 如果你是开发者，想本地运行、修改代码甚至贡献 feature： 1. 克隆仓库： bash git clone cd open-canvas 2. 安装依赖并启动： bash pnpm install pnpm dev 3. 打开 4. 在页面里填入你的 Cyberbara API Key，或者参考 .env.example 配置你自己的本地 S3 兼容对象存储，即可实现完全的“本地自给自足”。 写在最后 目前 Open Canvas 还处于 alpha 阶段，模型列表（model catalog）和模型 schema 的动态表单等功能还在路线图里逐步完善。它算不上十全十美，但它足够简单、轻量、且完全开源。 我希望通过这个项目，能帮大家打破高昂的创作壁垒，用最低的成本（几毛钱生图、生视频）去拼装出属于自己的 AI 工作流。如果你也喜欢这个方向，欢迎来 GitHub 提 Issue 或 PR，我们一起把它变得更好玩。 项目 GitHub ZeroLu/open-canvas （觉得不错的话，顺手给个 Star 支持一下，感激不尽！） 在线试用：

projects.title: Show HN: Riley – Content That Sounds Like You, Not Like AI
projects.author: vacostacambas
projects.summary: Working for a US company with several, very different, lines of business taught me how difficult it is to post on social media consistently and keeping the essence of each brand in all posts. Standard AI tools helped me get the first draft, but that was it. I would spend hours editing the output to make it sound a bit more like me, but in the end this was more time-consuming than starting from a blank page. Tired of choosing between consistency and maintaining the brand’s essence and my voice, I built Riley. My goal was to teach AI how I sound and the essence of each brand to remove endless prompts and constant tweaking, keep creative momentum, and make content creation a smooth and enjoyable process. Riley learns from previous content you’ve written to generate pieces that sounds like you, not like AI. You can import examples (LinkedIn posts, website copy, social media, etc.), define context with @context-pills for background, audience, and style, and refine with feedback and comments. With one-line prompts, Riley outputs tailored pieces for multiple platforms at once while adapting over time. The more you teach Riley with feedback, the better she’ll write. Riley learns your style by extracting patterns from your imported writing and ongoing edits/comments, such as vocabulary, sentence rhythm, tone preferences, structures, and what to avoid. No need to actually explain to her “how you write,” she will know the more you work with her. This becomes persistent context that informs every generation, rather than one-off instructions. How is Riley different from ChatGPT or Claude? Standard LLMs require repeating lengthy context in every new session, and if you ask the model to create several pieces at once, the LLM will most likely write 2-3 really good pieces, and then start creating content you wish the LLM had never written. Claude and ChatGPT (and all other LLMs) don’t retain or iteratively improve from your feedback across conversations in the same seamless, workspace-based way. Riley keeps your writing DNA and style active and refines it continuously. Looking for feedback about (1) onboarding flow, (2) platform UX/UI, (3) how well Riley preserves nuances of personal/brand voice, (4) features you’d like to see in Riley, (5) anything else you can think of. Thank you HN community!

projects.title: 〖网站自荐〗LitSource：面向医学论文写作的真实文献核验与论点溯源工具
projects.author: yandong2023
projects.summary: 〖网站自荐〗LitSource：面向医学论文写作的真实文献核验与论点溯源工具 大家好，我是 LitSource 的开发者。最近做了一个和医学论文写作有关的小工具，想推荐给周刊读者。 网站地址： LitSource 是一个面向医学与生命科学写作的文献核验工具。它主要做两件事： 1. 根据一句医学论点，反查真实存在的相关论文； 2. 检查参考文献是否真实、是否能支撑正文里的观点。 为什么做这个工具？ 现在很多人都会用 AI 辅助写论文、综述、开题报告。 AI 写正文的能力已经很强了，一段话看起来也很像论文。但是在医学写作里，最麻烦的问题不是“这句话写得像不像”，而是： 这句话背后的文献到底是不是真的？ 这篇文献到底支不支持这个观点？ AI 给出的参考文献是不是编出来的？ 医学和生命科学对文献真实性要求很高。 一篇不存在的论文、一个错配的 DOI，或者一条并不能支撑正文观点的引用，都可能带来很严重的问题。 我最开始注意到这个需求，是因为看到很多人用 AI 写综述时，正文写得很快，但最后还要花大量时间一条条核对参考文献。尤其是 AI 生成的 Reference，有些看起来非常真实，但去 PubMed、Crossref 或期刊官网查时，发现标题、作者、DOI、年份并不匹配，甚至整篇文献根本不存在。 所以我想做的不是另一个“AI 帮你写论文”的工具，而是一个更靠后的环节： AI 可以辅助写作，但引用必须回到真实文献。 功能一：根据论点反查真实文献 很多论文写作场景里，用户已经有了一个观点，但不知道该引用哪篇文献。 比如你写了一句话： 某种治疗方法可能改善某类患者的预后。 这时候最需要的不是让 AI 随便编几篇参考文献，而是找到真实存在、可以被核验的论文。 LitSource 支持输入一句中文或英文医学论点，系统会去匹配真实学术来源，并返回相关论文、DOI、PMID、期刊、年份等信息。 功能二：区分支持、反对和相关论文 我觉得这也是 LitSource 里比较重要的一个功能。 医学论文写作不是只找“支持自己观点”的文献。很多时候，真正有价值的是知道： 哪些论文支持这个观点； 哪些论文可能反对这个观点； 哪些论文只是背景相关，但不能直接当作证据引用。 所以 LitSource 在返回结果时，会尽量把文献按照“支持 / 反对 / 相关”进行区分，帮助用户更快判断这些论文和当前论点之间的关系。 这个功能的目标不是替用户下最终结论，而是帮助用户更快建立证据链。 尤其是在写综述、讨论部分、研究背景时，单纯堆文献不够，知道不同研究之间的证据方向更重要。 功能三：参考文献真实性核验 另一个常见场景是：用户已经有了一份 Reference 列表，但不确定里面有没有 AI 幻觉文献。 LitSource 支持把参考文献列表粘贴进去，系统会检查标题、作者、DOI、期刊、年份等信息是否匹配，并尽量返回可点击的原始来源。 它适合在这些场景使用： AI 生成论文草稿后，检查参考文献是否真实； 投稿前核对 Reference 列表； 导师或编辑审稿前，快速发现可疑引用； 写综述时，避免把错配文献当作证据引用。 功能四：句子级证据定位 很多搜索工具会返回一篇论文，但用户还要自己打开摘要、全文、结果部分慢慢找。 LitSource 会尽量定位到和论点相关的证据句，让用户更快判断这篇文献是否真的有用。 这样用户不是只知道“这篇论文相关”，而是能更快看到： 它到底是哪句话、哪一段，可能支撑或反驳了当前论点。 和普通 AI 写作工具有什么不同？ LitSource 不想替用户直接写论文，也不鼓励把论文完全交给 AI 生成。 它更像是一个“文献真实性检查器”和“证据链辅助工具”。 医学论文里的引用不是装饰。 如果引用是假的，或者引用和观点不匹配，那么正文写得再漂亮也没有意义。 所以 LitSource 更关注这些问题： 文献是否真实存在； 元数据是否匹配； 这篇文献到底支持、反对，还是只是相关； 论点背后有没有可追溯的真实来源； 参考文献列表里有没有 AI 幻觉文献。 免费使用 目前 LitSource 每个月都会提供一定的免费积分，普通用户可以直接试用基础功能，不需要一上来就付费。 我希望先让更多医学、生命科学、科研写作相关的用户真实体验这个工具，再根据反馈继续优化。 适合哪些人？ 医学生、研究生、博士生； 医学论文、综述、开题报告作者； 使用 AI 写论文，但担心参考文献不可靠的人； 需要根据一句论点快速找到真实文献的人； 需要检查 Reference 是否存在伪引、错引的人； 医学编辑、导师、科研团队。 最后 AI 让论文写作变快了，但医学论文不能只追求“写得快”。 真正重要的是： 每一个关键论点背后，都应该有真实、可查、能支撑它的文献。 LitSource 想做的就是这个中间环节： 帮用户把 AI 写作和真实文献之间的证据链补上。 网站地址： 欢迎大家试用，也欢迎医学、生命科学、科研写作方向的朋友给我反馈。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】self-media-compliance-review：自媒体内容发布前的合规风险审核 Skill
projects.author: JuneYaooo
projects.summary: 最近开始做自媒体，发现一个挺常见但又很难排查的问题：内容有时候不知道为什么就违规了。 有些问题在官方规则里能找到依据，但更多时候，只有等到被限流、下架、提示违规，或者申诉失败之后，才慢慢从别人的经验里知道可能踩了什么点。 所以我整理了一个开源的 Agent Skill： 它主要做两件事。 第一，收录各个平台的官方规则说明，目前包括视频号、微信公众号、抖音、快手、B站、小红书等平台。 第二，整理社交媒体上创作者讨论过的违规案例、申诉经验、评论回复和一些疑似“隐形规则”的线索。官方规则是主要依据，创作者讨论只作为辅助参考，用来帮助排查那些规则没有写得很细、但实际发布时经常遇到的问题。 使用时，可以让支持 Skills 的 AI Agent 帮忙做违规答疑，或者在内容发布前做一遍风险检查。比如检查标题、封面、字幕、口播、商品链接、发布文案里有没有比较明显的风险点。 这个项目不是法律意见，也不能保证平台一定审核通过。它更像是一个发布前的自查清单和经验库，帮助自己在发布前多看一遍，也希望能帮助大家更好、更安全地做自媒体。 开源出来也是想邀请大家一起补充：各个平台的新规则、真实踩坑案例、申诉经验、整改方式，以及哪些说法容易被误判。
